_comment: One job per STRIP — the whole strip as one image, for the concept run. Run with comic_render.py --provider runway|google|openai.

jobs.title: Drift Wood #36 · Most Likely, again
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 19, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, chin up, unkempt dark hair falling forward, sharp jaw; CHLOE — aged 19, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders; GULLY — aged 20, stocky boy with a round face, easy slouch. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Senior superlatives, the real ones. He wins. The strip is drawn the normal size. Panel 1: a high school gym awards assembly seen from the bleachers, a principal at a microphone under a CLASS OF 1999 banner, three teenagers in a middle row (in this panel: WOOD, CHLOE, GULLY). Principal says "...Most Likely to Win a Pulitzer: Arthur Finch.". Panel 2: a gaunt teenage boy in an oversized overcoat standing up in the bleachers with no expression amid small applause marks (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: close-up of a teenage girl clapping and looking straight ahead while speaking sideways to someone (in this panel: CHLOE). Chloe says "Don't say anything.". Wood says "I wasn't going to.". Chloe says "You were going to quote someone.". Wood says "...Daumier.". Panel 4: an empty high school gym after an assembly with a single certificate left lying on a bleacher, wide and quiet, black and white, no words. No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
